note: Ground truth for scripts/evaluate.py. 'expect.verdict' is the session verdict ThreadLens must produce; 'must' lists finding classifications that must appear, 'must_not' those that must not.

scenarios.title: Bank transfer deadlock
scenarios.description: Two tellers transfer money in opposite directions. Each locks the source account, then the destination account, so the lock order is inverted between them.
scenarios.teaches: Circular wait, hold-and-wait, the four Coffman conditions.

scenarios.title: Bank transfer — consistent lock order (fix)
scenarios.description: Same program; transfer() always locks the lower account id first, which breaks the circular-wait condition.
scenarios.teaches: Global lock ordering as deadlock prevention.

scenarios.title: Bank transfer deadlock (C++ std::mutex)
scenarios.description: The same bug written with std::thread, std::mutex and nested std::lock_guard objects. std::mutex is a pthread mutex underneath, so no source changes are needed for monitoring.
scenarios.teaches: C++ RAII locks still deadlock when the order is inconsistent.

scenarios.title: Bank transfer — std::scoped_lock (C++ fix)
scenarios.description: Both mutexes are acquired with C++17 std::scoped_lock, whose lock/try_lock/back-off algorithm cannot deadlock. Try-lock acquisitions do not create lock-order edges.
scenarios.teaches: Deadlock avoidance by acquiring all locks at once.

scenarios.title: Healthy workers
scenarios.description: Four workers update shared statistics with short critical sections and a consistently ordered nested lock.
scenarios.teaches: What correct, low-contention locking looks like.

scenarios.title: Hot lock contention
scenarios.description: Eight workers keep one lock for ~2 ms each time. Threads spend most of their time waiting, but the program always finishes.
scenarios.teaches: Contention is a performance problem, not a deadlock.

scenarios.title: Producer–consumer (condition variables)
scenarios.description: Bounded buffer with not_full / not_empty condition variables. Waits are inside while loops that re-check the predicate.
scenarios.teaches: pthread_cond_wait releases and re-acquires the mutex.

scenarios.title: Lock-order inversion (potential, single run)
scenarios.description: One thread takes lock_a then lock_b, another takes lock_b then lock_a, but a hand-off serializes them, so this run completes. The lock-order graph still contains the cycle.
scenarios.teaches: Potential vs. confirmed deadlock; GoodLock-style prediction.

scenarios.title: Lock order A→B (cross-run part 1)
scenarios.description: Takes lock_a then lock_b only. Harmless on its own; combine with the B→A run in the cross-run lock-order analysis.
scenarios.teaches: Merging lock-order graphs from separate executions.

scenarios.title: Lock order B→A (cross-run part 2)
scenarios.description: Takes lock_b then lock_a only. Together with an A→B session the merged lock-order graph has a cycle.
scenarios.teaches: Merging lock-order graphs from separate executions.

scenarios.title: Thread lifecycle
scenarios.description: Threads that return, call pthread_exit, detach themselves, are cancelled inside pthread_cond_wait, and create/join a grandchild.
scenarios.teaches: Thread creation, joining, detaching, cancellation and cleanup handlers.

scenarios.title: Mutex misuse and error codes
scenarios.description: EDEADLK on error-checking relock, EPERM on foreign unlock, EBUSY on destroying a locked mutex, abandoned normal and robust mutexes.
scenarios.teaches: Mutex types (normal, recursive, error-checking, robust) and their error semantics.

scenarios.title: Self-deadlock (relocking a normal mutex)
scenarios.description: A thread locks a normal (non-recursive) mutex that it already holds and waits for itself forever.
scenarios.teaches: Self-loops in the wait-for graph; recursive vs. normal mutexes.

scenarios.title: Dining philosophers (deadlock)
scenarios.description: Five philosophers each pick up the left fork and then the right fork: a five-thread circular wait.
scenarios.teaches: Cycles longer than two; Dijkstra's classic problem.

scenarios.title: Dining philosophers — resource ordering (fix)
scenarios.description: Every philosopher picks up the lower-numbered fork first, so the cycle cannot close.

scenarios.title: Join while holding a lock
scenarios.description: main holds config_lock and joins a worker that needs config_lock: the cycle mixes a join edge and a lock edge.
scenarios.teaches: Wait-for edges are not only mutexes: thread joins can close a cycle.

scenarios.title: Lost wake-up (condition-variable stall)
scenarios.description: A signal is sent before anybody waits and the waiter does not re-check the predicate, so it waits forever. There is no lock cycle; ThreadLens reports a stall with an inconclusive cause.
scenarios.teaches: Why condition-variable waits need a predicate loop; limits of wait-for graphs.

scenarios.title: High event-rate stress
scenarios.description: 8 threads × 20 000 iterations over 16 mutexes with ordered nesting (~600 000 events). Used for throughput, event-loss and overhead measurements; run without the collector for the baseline.
